stem.text: The concentration of a medicine in a patient's blood is modeled by a differentiable function C of time t, measured in hours, whose rate of change is \( C'(t) = \frac{65 e^{- \frac{t}{6}}}{6} \) milligrams per liter per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 18 \). Using a calculator, find \( C'(3) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( C'(3) = 6.571 \), so at time t = 3 hours the concentration of the medicine is increasing at a rate of 6.571 milligrams per liter per hour.

worked_solution.text: With a calculator, \( C'(3) = 6.571 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so at time t = 3 hours the concentration of the medicine is increasing at a rate of 6.571 milligrams per liter per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change

options.derivation: the rate of change of a non-motion quantity called a velocity
